content: Aspirin is a common medication used for pain relief, reducing fever, and inflammation. It also acts as an antiplatelet drug, preventing blood clots (used for heart attack/stroke risk reduction). Available in regular, enteric-coated, and low-dose forms. Dosage varies by purpose (e.g., 81–100 mg daily for heart protection vs. higher doses for pain). Side effects may include stomach irritation, ulcers, or bleeding risks.
